planeModel.offsetFormula: ds = solid.verts . n; d = min(ds) + (offsetBase + offsetSpan*height/100)*(max(ds)-min(ds))

PLANE.note: the cut face this plane produces is the target outline

axis_aligned_default.note: the obvious straight cut at the same height: the knife was never tilted

cut_too_low.note: the right angle of cut, stopped short below the target height

cut_too_high.note: the right angle of cut, pushed past the target height

under_tilted.note: tilted, but not far enough: the cut face stops short of the target outline

over_tilted.note: tilted past the target: the cut face runs off the wrong faces of the solid

planeModel.offsetFormula: ds = solid.verts . n; d = min(ds) + (offsetBase + offsetSpan*height/100)*(max(ds)-min(ds))

PLANE.note: the cut face this plane produces is the target outline

axis_aligned_default.note: the obvious straight cut at the same height: the knife was never tilted

cut_too_low.note: the right angle of cut, stopped short below the target height

cut_too_high.note: the right angle of cut, pushed past the target height

under_tilted.note: tilted, but not far enough: the cut face stops short of the target outline

over_tilted.note: tilted past the target: the cut face runs off the wrong faces of the solid

mirrored_twist.note: the same tilt turned the other way: the cut face is the mirror image of the target

scoring.rule: p = planeFor(content.solid, response.plane.h, response.plane.t, response.plane.w) using content.planeModel; o = outlineOf(section(content.solid, p), p); correct iff o.length === answer.vertexCount AND shapeDistance(o, answer.targetSignature) <= answer.shapeToleranceRms. shapeDistance minimises RMS vertex distance over cyclic shifts after the closed-form Procrustes rotation; it is scale- and chirality-sensitive, so a mirror image of the target is rejected. Responses are quantised to content.controls.step, so the accepted set is finite and the verdict is exactly reproducible.
scoring.partialCredit: M-POLY = shapeDistance(o, answer.targetSignature); lower is closer.

planeModel.normalFormula: a = tilt/100*tiltMaxRad; b = twist/100*twistMaxRad; n = unit(sin a*cos b, cos a, sin a*sin b)
planeModel.offsetFormula: ds = solid.verts . n; d = min(ds) + (offsetBase + offsetSpan*height/100)*(max(ds)-min(ds))

PLANE.note: the cut face this plane produces is the target outline

axis_aligned_default.note: the obvious straight cut at the same height: the knife was never tilted

cut_too_low.note: the right angle of cut, stopped short below the target height

cut_too_high.note: the right angle of cut, pushed past the target height

under_tilted.note: tilted, but not far enough: the cut face stops short of the target outline

wrong_twist.note: right height and tilt, plane turned about the wrong axis

scoring.rule: p = planeFor(content.solid, response.plane.h, response.plane.t, response.plane.w) using content.planeModel; o = outlineOf(section(content.solid, p), p); correct iff o.length === answer.vertexCount AND shapeDistance(o, answer.targetSignature) <= answer.shapeToleranceRms. shapeDistance minimises RMS vertex distance over cyclic shifts after the closed-form Procrustes rotation; it is scale- and chirality-sensitive, so a mirror image of the target is rejected. Responses are quantised to content.controls.step, so the accepted set is finite and the verdict is exactly reproducible.
